A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GMG research, with matching authors, methods, theoretical results and benchmarks. Their complete main texts, figures, tables and appendices support comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic transport experiments and disentanglement results on four image benchmarks, including encoder/decoder ablations and decoder-free learning.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark and decoder-free results and additionally reports encoder configurations and gradient-stability experiments.

M1.justification: The proposed method remains distortion minus Gromov-Wasserstein cost, incorporated into VAE objectives through encoder or decoder regularization. The same geometric cost families remain, with IR/SIR/CR renamed L2-squared/ScL2-squared/Cos. New pseudocode and implementation details do not establish an underlying algorithm change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Shapes3D, DSprites, SmallNORB and Cars3D, retain the synthetic transport examples, and report decoder-free learning on Shapes3D. The new gradient analyses reuse these datasets without introducing a distinct task or population.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparison methods remain beta-VAE and beta-TCVAE, each with optional HFS, together with distortion and Jacobian-based regularization. New encoder experiments extend configurations of these methods. Newly cited related works do not become additional evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: v2 introduces gradient-alignment evaluation using a fixed, randomly initialized, untrained network and five minibatches per dataset (Appendix C.2). Encoder distance-cost configurations are added and the joint 0.5/0.5 configuration disappears. Appendix C.1 replaces v1's stated active regularization weight of 1 with a varying weight, although both already report the same search grid; rerunning is not established. Architecture, batch size 64, 300,000 training steps and DCI-D remain.

E4.justification: v2 adds a substantial stability investigation comparing encoder and decoder gradients across all four datasets (Figures 3–4). Table 1 extends encoder ablations from cosine to squared and scaled squared distances. Conversely, the joint encoder–decoder ablations in v1 Table 4 are removed. The decoder-free analysis is retained in Appendix D.3.

E5.justification: v1 already reports uncertainty and specifies five seeds for Shapes3D Table 1. v2 explicitly identifies benchmark entries as means and standard deviations over five seeds, and adds distributions of gradient alignment across five sampled batches. This expands statistical reporting without establishing an increase in training runs.

E6.justification: Most previously reported decoder and decoder-free scores are retained. v2 adds encoder distance-cost results and gradient-alignment findings, with a particularly clear decoder-alignment advantage on DSprites. The Shapes3D beta-VAE decoder GMG entry with squared-distance costs changes from 72.0 ±12.5 to 72.0 ±8.5. Joint encoder–decoder result rows are removed.

T1.justification: The central weak-convexity theorem and most derivations remain (v1 Theorem 3.7; v2 Theorem 3.5). v2 makes admissible-kernel assumptions explicit, qualifies the GM/GW optimality-gap interpretation, and adds zero-gap sufficiency and cost-rescaling proofs in B.1–B.2. Its consistency proposition is narrowed to squared Euclidean and inner-product costs, omitting v1's explicit scaling and cosine extension.

C1.justification: The GMG, weak-convexity and four-benchmark contributions remain. v2 centers its abstract and introduction on reconciling prior matching with minimal geometric distortion. Decoder-free learning and prospective scalability cease to be headline contributions, although their experiment and exploratory claims remain in Appendix D.3.

C2.justification: v1 emphasizes distortion's conflict with reconstruction; v2 emphasizes its conflict with prior alignment. v2 adds explanations connecting cosine regularization to latent expressiveness and GMG debiasing to gradient stability. The joint-regularization interpretation disappears, while the decoder-free limitation favoring DST remains. Broad GMG-dominance wording needs qualification because some new encoder rows favor DST.

D1.justification: Algorithm 1 and Appendix E substantially expand implementation disclosure: cost-dependent entropy scaling, epsilon scale 0.1, mean-based normalization, uniform coupling initialization and implementation code. Appendix C.2 specifies the stability procedure. Existing VAE architecture and hardware details remain. However, the printed code is not directly runnable: stat_fn follows default arguments without a default, and scale_cost_x is read before assignment.

R1.justification: v2 acknowledges concurrent GMG work by Sotiropoulou and Alvarez-Melis and distinguishes its disentanglement application and theoretical investigation. It expands geometric/topological related work, including Hahm, Moor and Balabin, and discusses flexibility relative to neural GW approaches. Some background OT citations, including Genevay and Pooladian, are removed.

P1.justification: The title is shortened and substantial portions of the introduction, background, method exposition and experimental narrative are rewritten. Duplicated introductory material is removed, contributions are enumerated, and experiments are organized around explicit questions. Proofs and appendices are reorganized, decoder-free learning moves to Appendix D.3, and a reproducibility section is added.

P2.justification: v2 adds a GMG schematic, Algorithm 1 and two gradient-stability figures. The original synthetic figure becomes Figure 2 with a revised caption. Table 1 integrates existing encoder results and new configurations; Table 2 removes the duplicated Shapes3D display. Ablation tables are reduced, the decoder-free table moves to the appendix, and typography, headers and page layout change throughout.

improvement.justification: v2 makes the existing contribution easier to understand and assess through clearer exposition, explicit concurrent-work positioning, solver details and relevant encoder/stability analyses. These are useful gains despite largely retained headline results. Their benefit is tempered by removal of the joint ablation, overbroad dominance wording and errors preventing Appendix E's code from running as printed. The net improvement is limited rather than substantial.
